narrative:
Based on your application, our model has determined there is a 56% chance you would be a bad credit risk, which is why your loan was denied. This decision was not made lightly, and we want to explain the specific factors that led to this outcome.

The most significant factor was your credit history. You have no credits or all previous credits have been paid off, which is a very uncommon profile among approved applicants—only about 2% of them share this background. This lack of a proven track record with credit made the model see you as a higher risk, pushing the decision toward denial.

Your checking account status also played a major role. With a balance between 0 and 200 Deutsche Marks, you fall into a category that is less common among approved applicants, where over half have no checking account at all. This limited financial buffer contributed to the perception of risk.

Interestingly, the amount you requested—4,280 DM—actually worked in your favor. While it is higher than the average approved loan of about 2,887 DM, the model viewed this as a positive sign, slightly pushing the prediction toward approval. However, this was not enough to overcome the negative impact of your credit history and account status.

Other aspects of your profile, like your 30-month loan duration (longer than the typical 19 months) and your installment rate of 4% of disposable income (above the average of 2.94%), also added to the overall risk assessment. Your situation as a renter and having two existing credits at the bank further contributed to the decision.

To improve your chances in the future, consider building a more established credit history by taking on smaller, manageable loans and paying them off consistently. Increasing your savings and maintaining a higher checking account balance would also help demonstrate financial stability. Finally, reducing your existing debt and opting for a shorter loan term could make your application more favorable.
